sources.authors: Lam WK, Maxwell JP, Masters RS.

findings.finding: Errorless learning procedures drastically lower the frequency of errors made during training sessions compared to conventional methods.
findings.quote: subjects trained with the errorless procedure averaged only 25 S− (errors) responses in the same number of sessions.

findings.finding: Practicing through an errorless learning protocol results in reduced verbal-analytical and motor planning region co-activation.
findings.quote: participants who practiced a golf putting task implicitly (via an errorless learning protocol) displayed less alpha2 T3-Fz co-activation than those who practiced explicitly

findings.finding: Beginning a task very close and moving progressively back reduces initial errors and lowers attention demands during subsequent execution.
findings.quote: Reducing errors during initial learning trials may encourage an implicit mode of learning and lower the demand for cognitive resources in subsequent performance.

principle: Structuring practice to minimize mistakes during learning reduces errors, lowers cognitive load, and supports implicit motor acquisition.
for_the_teacher: Start learners very close or at a very slow, manageable version of a movement and gradually increase the distance, speed, or difficulty so they experience virtually no errors.
when_it_does_not_apply: Some evidence suggests that learners given errorless training can be very slow to make a discrimination reversal, and errorless procedures may not always successfully minimize errors in certain perceptual motor tasks.
